questions.solution:

Compare the measured count to the zero-tolerance standard.

**Answer.** Fails / unsafe

questions.stem: In a nitrifying reactor the ammonia-nitrogen falls from $40\,\text{mg/L}$ to $6\,\text{mg/L}$ as it is oxidised to nitrate. Taking the stoichiometric requirement as $4.57\,\text{g O}_2$ per g of N nitrified, the oxygen demand exerted by nitrification is _____ mg/L.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Nitrification (NH₄⁺ → NO₃⁻) consumes 4.57 g O₂ per g N. Demand $=\Delta N\times4.57$.

**Working.**
$$(40-6)\times4.57=155.38\,\text{mg/L}.$$

**Answer.** $155.38\,\text{mg/L}$

questions.subject: Environmental Microbiology
questions.stem: Which processes are strictly anaerobic in wastewater treatment?
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Methanogenesis requires strict anaerobiosis. Denitrification is anoxic (uses NO₃⁻), nitrification and carbon oxidation are aerobic.

**Working.**
Only methanogenesis is strictly anaerobic.

**Answer.** Methanogenesis

questions.solution:
**Concept.** $F/M=\dfrac{Q\cdot S_0}{V\cdot X}$.

**Working.**
$$F/M=\dfrac{0.5\times10^6\times250\times10^{-6}}{1000\times3.0\times10^{-3}}=\dfrac{125}{3}=41.67\,\text{(incorrect units)}.$$
Re-check: $Q=0.5\,\text{MLD}$, $S_0=250\,\text{g/m}^3$, $V=1000\,\text{m}^3$, $X=3000\,\text{g/m}^3$.
$$F/M=\dfrac{0.5\times10^6\times250}{1000\times3000}=\dfrac{125{,}000{,}000}{3{,}000{,}000}=0.0417.$$

Assuming zero-order kinetics within the biofilm ($S_b\gg K_s$), the substrate flux $J$ into the biofilm is _____ mg/(cm$^2$·s).

questions.subject: Environmental Microbiology
questions.stem: For a biofilm, the maximum volumetric substrate utilization rate $k_0=8\,\text{kg/(m}^3\text{·d)}$, effective diffusivity $D_e=1.0\times10^{-9}\,\text{m}^2$/s, half-saturation $K_s=5\,\text{g/m}^3$, and bulk substrate $S_b=20\,\text{g/m}^3$. The Thiele modulus $\phi$ is _____.
questions.solution:
**Concept.** $\phi=L_f\sqrt{\dfrac{k_0}{D_e\,S_b}}$ simplified as $\phi=\sqrt{\dfrac{k_0}{D_e\,S_b/L_f^2}}$, for a first-order approximation: $\phi=\sqrt{\dfrac{k_0\,K_s}{D_e\,S_b}}$.
Using $\phi=\sqrt{\dfrac{k_0}{D_e\,S_b}}$ with consistent units: $k_0=8\,\text{kg/(m}^3\text{·d)}=9.26\times10^{-5}\,\text{g/(cm}^3\text{·s)}$.

**Working.** Simplified: $\phi=\sqrt{\dfrac{k_0}{D_e\,S_b/K_s}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{8}{1.0\times10^{-9}\times86400\times4}}=\sqrt{\dfrac{8}{3.456\times10^{-4}}}=\sqrt{23148}=152.1.$
Note: exact value depends on length-scale convention; this uses a common formulation.

**Answer.** $\approx 152$

questions.subject: Environmental Microbiology
questions.stem: Which factors increase the grazing pressure of protozoa on bacteria in activated sludge?
questions.solution:
**Concept.** Protozoan grazing increases with higher protozoan density, higher bacterial concentration (up to saturation), and longer SRT. High pH inhibits protozoa.

**Answer.** Higher protozoan density, Higher bacterial concentration, Longer sludge retention time
